L22: arXiv:1912.04683v2 [math.NT] 06 Jan 2023
L23: # A variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus
L24: 
L25: Tomos Parry
L26: ## 1 -  Introduction
L27: 
L28: Let
L29: 
L30:  | $$\mathcal{S}=\{n\in\mathbb{N}|\text{ there is no prime $p$ with }p^{k}|n\},$$  |
L31: 
L32: the set of $k$-free numbers. For some suitable main term $\eta(q,a)$ to be defined soon enough we will study in this paper the object
L33: 
L34:  | $$\sum_{a=1}^{q}\left(\sum_{n\leq x\atop{n\in\mathcal{S}\atop{n\equiv a\text{ mod }(q)}}}1-x\eta(q,a)\right)^{2},$$  |
L35: a variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions when averaging over a (complete) residue system. One would like to establish for some $q$ that this is
L36: 
L37:  | $$\approx q\left(\frac{x}{q}\right)^{1/k}$$  |
L38: 
L39: since this would mean that on average
L40: 
L41:  | $$\sum_{n\leq x\atop{n\in\mathcal{S}\atop{n\equiv a\text{ mod }(q)}}}1-x\eta(q,a)\approx\left(\frac{x}{q}\right)^{1/2k}.$$  |  | (1)
L42: 
L43: Since an improvement in the error term in the classical statement
L44:  | $$\sum_{n\leq x\atop{n\in\mathcal{S}}}1=\frac{x}{\zeta(k)}+\mathcal{O}\left(x^{1/k}\right)$$  |
L45: 
L46: is tantamount to a better zero-free region for the zeta function, information as to the true size of the LHS of (【9†1】) is relevant.
L47: Averaging just over the reduced classes an asymptotic formula for the variance, in the squarefree case, is already established in [【10†3】] with error essentially
L48: 
L49:  | $$\ll q\left(\frac{x}{q}\right)^{1/3}+\bigg(\frac{x}{q}\bigg)^{23/15}.$$  |  | (2)
L50: Before this only upper bound results are recorded (see [【11†1】] and the references therein), although these are stronger in the range where the above asymptotic formulas don’t hold and are concerned with more general sequences than the squarefrees. In this paper, we improve the first error term in (【12†2】).
L51: ###### Theorem.
L52: 
L53: Let $k\geq 2$ and denote by $\mathcal{S}$ the set of $k$-free numbers. For $q,a\in\mathbb{N}$ and $x>0$ define
L54: 
L55:  | $\displaystyle\eta(q,a)=\sum_{d=1\atop{(q,d^{k})|a}}^{\infty}\frac{\mu(d)}{[q,d^{k}]},\hskip 28.45274ptE_{x}(q,a)=\sum_{n\leq x\atop{n\in\mathcal{S}\atop{n\equiv a(q)}}}1-x\eta(q,a)\hskip 42.67912pt$  |  | (3)
L56: 
L57: and
L58: 
L59:  | $$V_{x}(q)=\sum_{a=1}^{q}|E_{x}(q,a)|^{2}.$$  |  | (4)
L60: 
L61: Define
L62: 
L63:  | $$C_{k}=\frac{2k}{(1/k-1)\zeta(2)}\prod_{p}\frac{1-2/(p^{k}+p^{k-1})}{1-p^{1-1/k}}$$  |
L64: and
L65: 
L66:  | $$f_{k}(q)=C_{k}\prod_{p|q}\frac{1-2/p^{k}+(q,p^{k})^{1/k-1}/p}{1-2/p^{k}+1/p}.$$  |
L67: 
L68: For $1\leq q\leq x$ we have for every $\epsilon>0$
L69: 
L70:  | $$V_{x}(q)=q\left(\frac{x}{q}\right)^{1/k}f_{k}(q)+\mathcal{O}_{k,\epsilon}\left(x^{\epsilon}\left(q\left(\frac{x}{q}\right)^{2/(9-2/k)}+\frac{x^{1+2/(k+1)}}{q}\right)\right).$$  |
L71: This is an asymptotic formula for $k=2,3,4$. The relevance of our result is the improvement in the first error term, which for $k=2$ seems decently small. This is obtained by a careful analysis of the integrals arising from an application of Perron’s formula. (Our second error term is weaker than in (【12†2】) but most likely can be made to be just as small for the squarefress by arguing, as in that paper, with the square sieve.)
L72: We consider $k\geq 2$ and $q\leq x$ as fixed throughout. Each time $\epsilon$ appears it is to be understood that it may be taken arbitrarily small at each occurence. Fix some $0<\delta<1/2k$. All $\ll,\mathcal{O}$ constants depend on $\epsilon,k$ and $\delta$.
L73: ## 2 -  Lemmas
L74: 
L75: For $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)>1$ define
L76: 
L77:  | $$\mathcal{F}(s)=\sum_{d,d^{\prime}=1}^{\infty}\frac{\mu(d)\mu(d^{\prime})}{[d^{k},d^{\prime k}][q,(d^{k},d^{\prime k})]^{s}}$$  |
L78: 
L79: and for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$ define
L80: 
L81:  | $$\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)=\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}\left(1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right)}\right).$$  |
L82: 
L83: The first series converges since the summands are bounded by
L84:  | $$\frac{1}{[d^{k},d^{\prime k}](d^{k},d^{\prime k})};$$  |
L85: 
L86: for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$
L87: 
L88:  | $\displaystyle\left|(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right|$  | $\displaystyle\leq$  | $\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}1/p^{k}&\text{ for }\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq 0\\
L89: 1/p^{k\delta}&\text{ for }\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)<0\end{array}\right.$  |  | (8)
L90:  |  | $\displaystyle\ll$  | $\displaystyle 1$  |
L91: 
L92: and therefore
L93: 
L94:  | $$1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\geq 1-1/2^{k\delta}\gg 1$$  |
L95: so that each Euler factor of the infinite product in $\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)$ is of the form
L96: 
L97:  | $$1+\mathcal{O}\left(1/p^{k}\right)$$  |
L98: 
L99: and therefore this product converges and is uniformly bounded for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$; for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$ we have
L100: 
L101:  | $$\frac{1}{p^{k(1+s)}}\geq\frac{1}{p^{k\delta}}$$  |
L102: 
L103: and therefore
L104: 
L105:  | $$1+1/p^{k(1+s)}\geq 1-1/2^{k\delta}\gg 1$$  |
L106: so each factor in the finite product in $\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)$ is from (【13†A variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus】) uniformly bounded for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$, and since we have just said the same is true for the infinite product, we conclude that $\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)\ll q^{\epsilon}$ for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$.
L107: ###### Lemma 2.1.
L108: 
L109: If $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)>1$ then
L110: 
L111:  | $$\mathcal{F}(s)=\frac{\zeta\left(k(s+1)\right)\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)}{q^{s}\zeta\left(2k(s+1)\right)}.$$  |
L112: ###### Proof.
L113: 
L114: We have
L115: 
L116:  | $\displaystyle\sum_{d,d^{\prime}}\frac{\mu(d)\mu(d^{\prime})(d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{1-s}(q,d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{s}}{d^{k}d^{\prime k}}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\sum_{N=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{N^{k}}\sum_{dd^{\prime}=N}\mu(d)\mu(d^{\prime})(d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{1-s}(q,d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{s}$  |  | (9)
L117:  |  | $\displaystyle=:$  | $\displaystyle\sum_{N=1}^{\infty}\frac{a_{q}(N)}{N^{k}}.$  |
L118: 
L119: Clearly $a_{q}(N)$ is multiplcative and simple calculations show
L120:  | $\displaystyle a_{q}(p)=-2,$  |
L121:  | $\displaystyle a_{q}(p^{2})=p^{k(1-s)}(q,p^{k})^{s}$  |
L122: 
L123: and $a_{q}(p^{t})=0$ for $t\geq 3$. Consequently
L124:  | $\displaystyle\sum_{N=1}^{\infty}\frac{a_{q}(N)}{N^{k}}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}}+\frac{(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)$  |  | (10)
L125:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p}\left(1+\frac{(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}\left(1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right)}\right)$  |
L126:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p}\left(1+\frac{1}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}\left(1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right)}\right)$  |
L127:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\frac{\zeta\left(k(1+s)\right)\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)}{\zeta\left(2k(1+s)\right)}$  |
L128: so that (【14†9】) becomes
L129: 
L130:  | $$\sum_{d,d^{\prime}}\frac{\mu(d)\mu(d^{\prime})(d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{1-s}(q,d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{s}}{d^{k}d^{\prime k}}=\frac{\zeta\left(k(1+s)\right)\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)}{\zeta\left(2k(1+s)\right)}$$  |
L131: 
L132: and the claim follows.∎
L133: ###### Lemma 2.2.
L134: 
L135: Suppose $q$ has $\omega$ distinct prime factors $p_{1},...,p_{\omega}$ and let $\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)$ be as given at the start of this section. Then for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and each $l_{1},..,l_{\omega},l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0$ there are $\lambda_{n},W_{n},C_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}},Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}\in\mathbb{R}$ with $W_{n},Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}>0$ such that
L136:  | $$\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)=\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}C_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}^{s}\lambda_{n}W_{n}^{1+s}$$  |
L137: 
L138: for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$. Moreover for $-1+\delta\leq\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\leq 0$
L139:  | $$\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left|C_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}^{s}\lambda_{n}W_{n}^{1+s}\right|\ll\log(q+1).$$  |
L140: ###### Proof.
L141: 
L142: From (【13†A variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus】) we have $|(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}|<1$ and therefore
L143: 
L144:  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}\left(1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right)}\right)$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}}\sum_{t\geq 1}\left(\frac{-(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)^{t-1}\right)$  |  | (11)
L145:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}f_{s}^{*}(n)$  |
L146: where $f^{*}_{s}(n)$ is the multiplicative function given on prime powers by
L147: 
L148:  | $$f_{s}^{*}(p^{t})=-\frac{2}{p^{k}}\left(\frac{-(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)^{t-1}.$$  |
L149: 
L150: For any $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and prime $p|n$ define $t=t(p)$ through $p^{t}||n$. Then
L151:  | $\displaystyle f^{*}_{s}(n)$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|n}\left(-\frac{2}{p^{k}}\right)\left(\frac{-(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)^{t-1}$  |  | (12)
L152:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\left(\prod_{p|n}(-1)^{t-1}\right)\left(\prod_{p|n}\frac{-2}{p^{k}}\right)\left(\prod_{p|n}(q,p^{k})^{-(t-1)}\right)\left(\prod_{p|n}\frac{(q,p^{k})^{(t-1)(1+s)}}{p^{(t-1)k(1+s)}}\right).\hskip 42.67912pt$  |
L153: 
L154: If we now define
L155:  | $$\lambda_{n}=\left(\prod_{p|n}(-1)^{t-1}\right)\left(\prod_{p|n}\frac{-2}{p^{k}}\right)\left(\prod_{p|n}(q,p^{k})^{1-t}\right)$$  |
L156: 
L157: and
L158: 
L159:  | $$W_{n}=\prod_{p|n}\frac{(q,p^{k})^{t-1}}{p^{(t-1)k}}$$  |
L160: 
L161: then (【15†12】) becomes
L162: 
L163:  | $$f^{*}(n)=\lambda_{n}W_{n}^{1+s}$$  |
L164: 
L165: so (【16†11】) becomes
L166: 
L167:  | $$\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}\left(1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right)}\right)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\lambda_{n}W_{n}^{1+s}.$$  |  | (13)
L168: 
L169: Just as (【16†11】) is true so is
L170:  | $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left|f_{s}^{*}(n)\right|=\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}}\sum_{t\geq 1}\left|\left(\frac{-(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)^{t-1}\right|\right).$$  |  | (14)
L171: 
L172: For $-1+\delta\leq\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\leq 0$ the $t$ sum here is from (【13†A variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus】)
L173: 
L174:  | $$\ll\sum_{t\geq 1}\left(\frac{1}{p^{k\delta}}\right)^{t-1}=\frac{1}{1-p^{k\delta}}\ll 1$$  |
L175: so the Euler product in (【17†14】) is uniformly bounded in this range and therefore
L176: 
L177:  | $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left|f^{*}(n)\right|\ll 1,\hskip 14.22636pt\text{ for }-1+\delta\leq\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\leq 0.$$  |  | (15)
L178: 
L179: We have for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$
L180: 
L181:  | $$\frac{1}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}=\sum_{l\geq 0}\left(\frac{-1}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)^{l}=\sum_{l\geq 0}\frac{C_{p}(l)}{p^{k(1+s)l}}$$  |  | (16)
L182: 
L183: for some $C_{p}(l)$ with
L184:  | $$\sum_{l\geq 0}\left|\frac{C_{p}(l)}{p^{k(1+s)l}}\right|\ll\sum_{l\geq 0}\left(\frac{1}{p^{k\delta}}\right)^{l}\ll 1.$$  |  | (17)
L185: 
L186: as well as
L187: 
L188:  | $$1+\frac{(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}=\sum_{l^{\prime}\geq 0}\frac{C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})(q,p^{k})^{sl^{\prime}}}{p^{k(1+s)l^{\prime}}}$$  |  | (18)
L189: 
L190: for some $C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})$ with
L191: 
L192:  | $$\sum_{l^{\prime}\geq 0}\left|\frac{C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})(q,p^{k})^{sl^{\prime}}}{p^{k(1+s)l^{\prime}}}\right|\leq 1+1.$$  |  | (19)
L193: from (【13†A variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus】). From (【18†16】), (【19†17】), (【20†18】) and (【21†19】) there are for each prime $p$ and $l,l^{\prime}\in\mathbb{N}$ some $C_{p}(l),C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})$ for which
L194: 
L195:  | $$\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}=\sum_{l,l^{\prime}\geq 0}\frac{C_{p}(l)C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})(q,p^{k})^{sl^{\prime}}}{p^{k(1+s)(l+l^{\prime})}}$$  |
L196: 
L197: and
L198:  | $$\sum_{l,l^{\prime}\geq 0}\left|\frac{C_{p}(l)C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})(q,p^{k})^{sl^{\prime}}}{p^{k(1+s)(l+l^{\prime})}}\right|\ll 1.$$  |
L199: 
L200: Consequently
L201:  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}\frac{C_{p_{1}}(l_{1})C_{p_{1}}^{\prime}(l_{1}^{\prime})\cdot\cdot\cdot C_{p_{\omega}}(l_{\omega})C_{p_{\omega}}^{\prime}(l_{\omega}^{\prime})(q,p_{1}^{k})^{sl_{1}^{\prime}}\cdot\cdot\cdot(q,p_{\omega}^{k})^{sl_{\omega}^{\prime}}}{p_{1}^{k(1+s)(l_{1}+l_{1}^{\prime})}\cdot\cdot\cdot p_{\omega}^{k(1+s)(l_{\omega}+l_{\omega}^{\prime})}}$  |
L202: and, for some $A>0$,
L203: 
L204:  | $$\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}\left|\frac{C_{p_{1}}(l_{1})C_{p_{1}}^{\prime}(l_{1}^{\prime})\cdot\cdot\cdot C_{p_{\omega}}(l_{\omega})C_{p_{\omega}}^{\prime}(l_{\omega}^{\prime})(q,p_{1}^{k})^{sl_{1}^{\prime}}\cdot\cdot\cdot(q,p_{\omega}^{k})^{sl_{\omega}^{\prime}}}{p_{1}^{k(1+s)(l_{1}+l_{1}^{\prime})}\cdot\cdot\cdot p_{\omega}^{k(1+s)(l_{\omega}+l_{\omega}^{\prime})}}\right|\leq A^{\omega}\ll\log(q+1)$$  |
L205: for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$. If we now define
L206:  | $$C^{*}_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}=\prod_{i=1}^{\omega}C_{p_{i}}(l_{i})C_{p_{i}}^{\prime}(l_{i}^{\prime}),\hskip 28.45274ptW_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}=\left(\prod_{i=1}^{\omega}p_{i}^{l_{i}+l_{i}^{\prime}}\right)^{k},\hskip 28.45274ptC_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}=\frac{C^{*}_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}}{W_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}},$$  |
L207:  | $$D_{\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}=\prod_{i=1}^{\omega}(q,p_{i}^{k})^{l_{i}^{\prime}},\hskip 14.22636pt\text{and}\hskip 14.22636ptZ_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}=\frac{D_{\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}}{W_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}}$$  |
L208: then
L209: 
L210:  | $$\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}=\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}C_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}^{s}$$  |
L211: 
L212: with
L213: 
L214:  | $\displaystyle\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}|C_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}^{s}|\ll\log(q+1)\hskip 28.45274pt$  |  | (20)
L215: for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$. The first claim now follows from (【22†13】) and the boundedness claim from (【23†15】) and (【24†20】). ∎
L216: ###### Lemma 2.3.
L217: 
L218: (A) Define
L219: 
L220:  | $$\alpha=\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}}+\frac{1}{p^{2k}}\right),$$  |
L221:  | $$\beta=\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{k}}\right)$$  |
L222: 
L223: and
L224: 
L225:  | $$\gamma=\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{-1+1/k}/p-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p-2/p^{k}}\prod_{p}\frac{1-2/(p^{k}+p^{k-1})}{1-p^{1-1/k}},$$  |
L226: 
L227: and let $\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)$ be as given at the start of this section. Then
L228:  | $$\frac{\zeta(2k)\mathcal{F}^{*}(1)}{\zeta(4k)}=\alpha,\hskip 14.22636pt\frac{\zeta(k)\mathcal{F}^{*}(0)}{\zeta(2k)}=\beta\hskip 14.22636pt\text{and}\hskip 14.22636pt\zeta(-1+1/k)\mathcal{F}^{*}(-1+1/k)=\gamma.$$  |
L229: 
L230: (B) Define $\eta(q,a)$ as in (【25†3】). For any $q,n\in\mathbb{N}$
L231: 
L232:  | $$\eta(q,n)=\eta\left(q,(q,n)\right)\ll q^{\epsilon-1}$$  |
L233: 
L234: and
L235: 
L236:  | $$\sum_{a=1}^{q}\eta(q,a)^{2}=\frac{\alpha}{q}.$$  |
L237: ###### Proof.
L238: 
L239: (A) So long as there are no problems with zeros of denominators we have
L240: 
L241:  | $\displaystyle\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}\prod_{p\not|\hskip 2.84526ptq}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}(1+1/p^{k(1+s)})}\right)$  |
L242:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}-2/p^{k}}\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}(1+1/p^{k(1+s)})}\right).$  |
L243: For $s=1,0,-1+1/k$ there are clearly no problems and therefore from the Euler product expressions for the Riemann zeta function
L244:  | $\displaystyle\frac{\zeta(2k)\mathcal{F}^{*}(1)}{\zeta(4k)}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}\prod_{p}\left(\frac{1-p^{-4k}}{1-p^{-2k}}\right)\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}(1+1/p^{2k})}\right)$  |
L245:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}\prod_{p}\left(1+\frac{1}{p^{2k}}-\frac{2}{p^{k}}\right),$  |

L23: # A variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus
L24: 
L25: Tomos Parry
L26: ## 1 -  Introduction
L27: 
L28: Let
L29: 
L30:  | $$\mathcal{S}=\{n\in\mathbb{N}|\text{ there is no prime $p$ with }p^{k}|n\},$$  |
L31: 
L32: the set of $k$-free numbers. For some suitable main term $\eta(q,a)$ to be defined soon enough we will study in this paper the object
L33: 
L34:  | $$\sum_{a=1}^{q}\left(\sum_{n\leq x\atop{n\in\mathcal{S}\atop{n\equiv a\text{ mod }(q)}}}1-x\eta(q,a)\right)^{2},$$  |
L35: a variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions when averaging over a (complete) residue system. One would like to establish for some $q$ that this is
L36: 
L37:  | $$\approx q\left(\frac{x}{q}\right)^{1/k}$$  |
L38: 
L39: since this would mean that on average
L40: 
L41:  | $$\sum_{n\leq x\atop{n\in\mathcal{S}\atop{n\equiv a\text{ mod }(q)}}}1-x\eta(q,a)\approx\left(\frac{x}{q}\right)^{1/2k}.$$  |  | (1)
L42: 
L43: Since an improvement in the error term in the classical statement
L44:  | $$\sum_{n\leq x\atop{n\in\mathcal{S}}}1=\frac{x}{\zeta(k)}+\mathcal{O}\left(x^{1/k}\right)$$  |
L45: 
L46: is tantamount to a better zero-free region for the zeta function, information as to the true size of the LHS of (【9†1】) is relevant.
L47: Averaging just over the reduced classes an asymptotic formula for the variance, in the squarefree case, is already established in [【10†3】] with error essentially
L48: 
L49:  | $$\ll q\left(\frac{x}{q}\right)^{1/3}+\bigg(\frac{x}{q}\bigg)^{23/15}.$$  |  | (2)
L50: Before this only upper bound results are recorded (see [【11†1】] and the references therein), although these are stronger in the range where the above asymptotic formulas don’t hold and are concerned with more general sequences than the squarefrees. In this paper, we improve the first error term in (【12†2】).
L51: ###### Theorem.
L52: 
L53: Let $k\geq 2$ and denote by $\mathcal{S}$ the set of $k$-free numbers. For $q,a\in\mathbb{N}$ and $x>0$ define
L54: 
L55:  | $\displaystyle\eta(q,a)=\sum_{d=1\atop{(q,d^{k})|a}}^{\infty}\frac{\mu(d)}{[q,d^{k}]},\hskip 28.45274ptE_{x}(q,a)=\sum_{n\leq x\atop{n\in\mathcal{S}\atop{n\equiv a(q)}}}1-x\eta(q,a)\hskip 42.67912pt$  |  | (3)
L56: 
L57: and
L58: 
L59:  | $$V_{x}(q)=\sum_{a=1}^{q}|E_{x}(q,a)|^{2}.$$  |  | (4)
L60: 
L61: Define
L62: 
L63:  | $$C_{k}=\frac{2k}{(1/k-1)\zeta(2)}\prod_{p}\frac{1-2/(p^{k}+p^{k-1})}{1-p^{1-1/k}}$$  |
L64: and
L65: 
L66:  | $$f_{k}(q)=C_{k}\prod_{p|q}\frac{1-2/p^{k}+(q,p^{k})^{1/k-1}/p}{1-2/p^{k}+1/p}.$$  |
L67: 
L68: For $1\leq q\leq x$ we have for every $\epsilon>0$
L69: 
L70:  | $$V_{x}(q)=q\left(\frac{x}{q}\right)^{1/k}f_{k}(q)+\mathcal{O}_{k,\epsilon}\left(x^{\epsilon}\left(q\left(\frac{x}{q}\right)^{2/(9-2/k)}+\frac{x^{1+2/(k+1)}}{q}\right)\right).$$  |
L71: This is an asymptotic formula for $k=2,3,4$. The relevance of our result is the improvement in the first error term, which for $k=2$ seems decently small. This is obtained by a careful analysis of the integrals arising from an application of Perron’s formula. (Our second error term is weaker than in (【12†2】) but most likely can be made to be just as small for the squarefress by arguing, as in that paper, with the square sieve.)
L72: We consider $k\geq 2$ and $q\leq x$ as fixed throughout. Each time $\epsilon$ appears it is to be understood that it may be taken arbitrarily small at each occurence. Fix some $0<\delta<1/2k$. All $\ll,\mathcal{O}$ constants depend on $\epsilon,k$ and $\delta$.
L73: ## 2 -  Lemmas
L74: 
L75: For $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)>1$ define
L76: 
L77:  | $$\mathcal{F}(s)=\sum_{d,d^{\prime}=1}^{\infty}\frac{\mu(d)\mu(d^{\prime})}{[d^{k},d^{\prime k}][q,(d^{k},d^{\prime k})]^{s}}$$  |
L78: 
L79: and for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$ define
L80: 
L81:  | $$\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)=\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}\left(1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right)}\right).$$  |
L82: 
L83: The first series converges since the summands are bounded by
L84:  | $$\frac{1}{[d^{k},d^{\prime k}](d^{k},d^{\prime k})};$$  |
L85: 
L86: for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$
L87: 
L88:  | $\displaystyle\left|(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right|$  | $\displaystyle\leq$  | $\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}1/p^{k}&\text{ for }\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq 0\\
L89: 1/p^{k\delta}&\text{ for }\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)<0\end{array}\right.$  |  | (8)
L90:  |  | $\displaystyle\ll$  | $\displaystyle 1$  |
L91: 
L92: and therefore
L93: 
L94:  | $$1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\geq 1-1/2^{k\delta}\gg 1$$  |
L95: so that each Euler factor of the infinite product in $\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)$ is of the form
L96: 
L97:  | $$1+\mathcal{O}\left(1/p^{k}\right)$$  |
L98: 
L99: and therefore this product converges and is uniformly bounded for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$; for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$ we have
L100: 
L101:  | $$\frac{1}{p^{k(1+s)}}\geq\frac{1}{p^{k\delta}}$$  |
L102: 
L103: and therefore
L104: 
L105:  | $$1+1/p^{k(1+s)}\geq 1-1/2^{k\delta}\gg 1$$  |
L106: so each factor in the finite product in $\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)$ is from (【13†A variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus】) uniformly bounded for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$, and since we have just said the same is true for the infinite product, we conclude that $\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)\ll q^{\epsilon}$ for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$.
L107: ###### Lemma 2.1.
L108: 
L109: If $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)>1$ then
L110: 
L111:  | $$\mathcal{F}(s)=\frac{\zeta\left(k(s+1)\right)\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)}{q^{s}\zeta\left(2k(s+1)\right)}.$$  |
L112: ###### Proof.
L113: 
L114: We have
L115: 
L116:  | $\displaystyle\sum_{d,d^{\prime}}\frac{\mu(d)\mu(d^{\prime})(d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{1-s}(q,d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{s}}{d^{k}d^{\prime k}}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\sum_{N=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{N^{k}}\sum_{dd^{\prime}=N}\mu(d)\mu(d^{\prime})(d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{1-s}(q,d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{s}$  |  | (9)
L117:  |  | $\displaystyle=:$  | $\displaystyle\sum_{N=1}^{\infty}\frac{a_{q}(N)}{N^{k}}.$  |
L118: 
L119: Clearly $a_{q}(N)$ is multiplcative and simple calculations show
L120:  | $\displaystyle a_{q}(p)=-2,$  |
L121:  | $\displaystyle a_{q}(p^{2})=p^{k(1-s)}(q,p^{k})^{s}$  |
L122: 
L123: and $a_{q}(p^{t})=0$ for $t\geq 3$. Consequently
L124:  | $\displaystyle\sum_{N=1}^{\infty}\frac{a_{q}(N)}{N^{k}}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}}+\frac{(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)$  |  | (10)
L125:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p}\left(1+\frac{(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}\left(1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right)}\right)$  |
L126:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p}\left(1+\frac{1}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}\left(1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right)}\right)$  |
L127:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\frac{\zeta\left(k(1+s)\right)\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)}{\zeta\left(2k(1+s)\right)}$  |
L128: so that (【14†9】) becomes
L129: 
L130:  | $$\sum_{d,d^{\prime}}\frac{\mu(d)\mu(d^{\prime})(d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{1-s}(q,d^{k},d^{\prime k})^{s}}{d^{k}d^{\prime k}}=\frac{\zeta\left(k(1+s)\right)\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)}{\zeta\left(2k(1+s)\right)}$$  |
L131: 
L132: and the claim follows.∎
L133: ###### Lemma 2.2.
L134: 
L135: Suppose $q$ has $\omega$ distinct prime factors $p_{1},...,p_{\omega}$ and let $\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)$ be as given at the start of this section. Then for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and each $l_{1},..,l_{\omega},l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0$ there are $\lambda_{n},W_{n},C_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}},Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}\in\mathbb{R}$ with $W_{n},Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}>0$ such that
L136:  | $$\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)=\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}C_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}^{s}\lambda_{n}W_{n}^{1+s}$$  |
L137: 
L138: for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$. Moreover for $-1+\delta\leq\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\leq 0$
L139:  | $$\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left|C_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}^{s}\lambda_{n}W_{n}^{1+s}\right|\ll\log(q+1).$$  |
L140: ###### Proof.
L141: 
L142: From (【13†A variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus】) we have $|(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}|<1$ and therefore
L143: 
L144:  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}\left(1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right)}\right)$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}}\sum_{t\geq 1}\left(\frac{-(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)^{t-1}\right)$  |  | (11)
L145:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}f_{s}^{*}(n)$  |
L146: where $f^{*}_{s}(n)$ is the multiplicative function given on prime powers by
L147: 
L148:  | $$f_{s}^{*}(p^{t})=-\frac{2}{p^{k}}\left(\frac{-(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)^{t-1}.$$  |
L149: 
L150: For any $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and prime $p|n$ define $t=t(p)$ through $p^{t}||n$. Then
L151:  | $\displaystyle f^{*}_{s}(n)$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|n}\left(-\frac{2}{p^{k}}\right)\left(\frac{-(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)^{t-1}$  |  | (12)
L152:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\left(\prod_{p|n}(-1)^{t-1}\right)\left(\prod_{p|n}\frac{-2}{p^{k}}\right)\left(\prod_{p|n}(q,p^{k})^{-(t-1)}\right)\left(\prod_{p|n}\frac{(q,p^{k})^{(t-1)(1+s)}}{p^{(t-1)k(1+s)}}\right).\hskip 42.67912pt$  |
L153: 
L154: If we now define
L155:  | $$\lambda_{n}=\left(\prod_{p|n}(-1)^{t-1}\right)\left(\prod_{p|n}\frac{-2}{p^{k}}\right)\left(\prod_{p|n}(q,p^{k})^{1-t}\right)$$  |
L156: 
L157: and
L158: 
L159:  | $$W_{n}=\prod_{p|n}\frac{(q,p^{k})^{t-1}}{p^{(t-1)k}}$$  |
L160: 
L161: then (【15†12】) becomes
L162: 
L163:  | $$f^{*}(n)=\lambda_{n}W_{n}^{1+s}$$  |
L164: 
L165: so (【16†11】) becomes
L166: 
L167:  | $$\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}\left(1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}\right)}\right)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\lambda_{n}W_{n}^{1+s}.$$  |  | (13)
L168: 
L169: Just as (【16†11】) is true so is
L170:  | $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left|f_{s}^{*}(n)\right|=\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}}\sum_{t\geq 1}\left|\left(\frac{-(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)^{t-1}\right|\right).$$  |  | (14)
L171: 
L172: For $-1+\delta\leq\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\leq 0$ the $t$ sum here is from (【13†A variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus】)
L173: 
L174:  | $$\ll\sum_{t\geq 1}\left(\frac{1}{p^{k\delta}}\right)^{t-1}=\frac{1}{1-p^{k\delta}}\ll 1$$  |
L175: so the Euler product in (【17†14】) is uniformly bounded in this range and therefore
L176: 
L177:  | $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left|f^{*}(n)\right|\ll 1,\hskip 14.22636pt\text{ for }-1+\delta\leq\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\leq 0.$$  |  | (15)
L178: 
L179: We have for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$
L180: 
L181:  | $$\frac{1}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}=\sum_{l\geq 0}\left(\frac{-1}{p^{k(1+s)}}\right)^{l}=\sum_{l\geq 0}\frac{C_{p}(l)}{p^{k(1+s)l}}$$  |  | (16)
L182: 
L183: for some $C_{p}(l)$ with
L184:  | $$\sum_{l\geq 0}\left|\frac{C_{p}(l)}{p^{k(1+s)l}}\right|\ll\sum_{l\geq 0}\left(\frac{1}{p^{k\delta}}\right)^{l}\ll 1.$$  |  | (17)
L185: 
L186: as well as
L187: 
L188:  | $$1+\frac{(q,p^{k})^{s}}{p^{k(1+s)}}=\sum_{l^{\prime}\geq 0}\frac{C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})(q,p^{k})^{sl^{\prime}}}{p^{k(1+s)l^{\prime}}}$$  |  | (18)
L189: 
L190: for some $C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})$ with
L191: 
L192:  | $$\sum_{l^{\prime}\geq 0}\left|\frac{C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})(q,p^{k})^{sl^{\prime}}}{p^{k(1+s)l^{\prime}}}\right|\leq 1+1.$$  |  | (19)
L193: from (【13†A variance for $k$-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus】). From (【18†16】), (【19†17】), (【20†18】) and (【21†19】) there are for each prime $p$ and $l,l^{\prime}\in\mathbb{N}$ some $C_{p}(l),C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})$ for which
L194: 
L195:  | $$\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}=\sum_{l,l^{\prime}\geq 0}\frac{C_{p}(l)C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})(q,p^{k})^{sl^{\prime}}}{p^{k(1+s)(l+l^{\prime})}}$$  |
L196: 
L197: and
L198:  | $$\sum_{l,l^{\prime}\geq 0}\left|\frac{C_{p}(l)C_{p}^{\prime}(l^{\prime})(q,p^{k})^{sl^{\prime}}}{p^{k(1+s)(l+l^{\prime})}}\right|\ll 1.$$  |
L199: 
L200: Consequently
L201:  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}\frac{C_{p_{1}}(l_{1})C_{p_{1}}^{\prime}(l_{1}^{\prime})\cdot\cdot\cdot C_{p_{\omega}}(l_{\omega})C_{p_{\omega}}^{\prime}(l_{\omega}^{\prime})(q,p_{1}^{k})^{sl_{1}^{\prime}}\cdot\cdot\cdot(q,p_{\omega}^{k})^{sl_{\omega}^{\prime}}}{p_{1}^{k(1+s)(l_{1}+l_{1}^{\prime})}\cdot\cdot\cdot p_{\omega}^{k(1+s)(l_{\omega}+l_{\omega}^{\prime})}}$  |
L202: and, for some $A>0$,
L203: 
L204:  | $$\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}\left|\frac{C_{p_{1}}(l_{1})C_{p_{1}}^{\prime}(l_{1}^{\prime})\cdot\cdot\cdot C_{p_{\omega}}(l_{\omega})C_{p_{\omega}}^{\prime}(l_{\omega}^{\prime})(q,p_{1}^{k})^{sl_{1}^{\prime}}\cdot\cdot\cdot(q,p_{\omega}^{k})^{sl_{\omega}^{\prime}}}{p_{1}^{k(1+s)(l_{1}+l_{1}^{\prime})}\cdot\cdot\cdot p_{\omega}^{k(1+s)(l_{\omega}+l_{\omega}^{\prime})}}\right|\leq A^{\omega}\ll\log(q+1)$$  |
L205: for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$. If we now define
L206:  | $$C^{*}_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}=\prod_{i=1}^{\omega}C_{p_{i}}(l_{i})C_{p_{i}}^{\prime}(l_{i}^{\prime}),\hskip 28.45274ptW_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}=\left(\prod_{i=1}^{\omega}p_{i}^{l_{i}+l_{i}^{\prime}}\right)^{k},\hskip 28.45274ptC_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}=\frac{C^{*}_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}}{W_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}},$$  |
L207:  | $$D_{\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}=\prod_{i=1}^{\omega}(q,p_{i}^{k})^{l_{i}^{\prime}},\hskip 14.22636pt\text{and}\hskip 14.22636ptZ_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}=\frac{D_{\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}}{W_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}}$$  |
L208: then
L209: 
L210:  | $$\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}=\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}C_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}^{s}$$  |
L211: 
L212: with
L213: 
L214:  | $\displaystyle\sum_{l_{1},...,l_{\omega}\geq 0\atop{l_{1}^{\prime},...,l_{\omega}^{\prime}\geq 0}}|C_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}Z_{\mathbf{l},\mathbf{l}^{\prime}}^{s}|\ll\log(q+1)\hskip 28.45274pt$  |  | (20)
L215: for $\mathfrak{R}\mathfrak{e}(s)\geq-1+\delta$. The first claim now follows from (【22†13】) and the boundedness claim from (【23†15】) and (【24†20】). ∎
L216: ###### Lemma 2.3.
L217: 
L218: (A) Define
L219: 
L220:  | $$\alpha=\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}}+\frac{1}{p^{2k}}\right),$$  |
L221:  | $$\beta=\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{k}}\right)$$  |
L222: 
L223: and
L224: 
L225:  | $$\gamma=\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{-1+1/k}/p-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p-2/p^{k}}\prod_{p}\frac{1-2/(p^{k}+p^{k-1})}{1-p^{1-1/k}},$$  |
L226: 
L227: and let $\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)$ be as given at the start of this section. Then
L228:  | $$\frac{\zeta(2k)\mathcal{F}^{*}(1)}{\zeta(4k)}=\alpha,\hskip 14.22636pt\frac{\zeta(k)\mathcal{F}^{*}(0)}{\zeta(2k)}=\beta\hskip 14.22636pt\text{and}\hskip 14.22636pt\zeta(-1+1/k)\mathcal{F}^{*}(-1+1/k)=\gamma.$$  |
L229: 
L230: (B) Define $\eta(q,a)$ as in (【25†3】). For any $q,n\in\mathbb{N}$
L231: 
L232:  | $$\eta(q,n)=\eta\left(q,(q,n)\right)\ll q^{\epsilon-1}$$  |
L233: 
L234: and
L235: 
L236:  | $$\sum_{a=1}^{q}\eta(q,a)^{2}=\frac{\alpha}{q}.$$  |
L237: ###### Proof.
L238: 
L239: (A) So long as there are no problems with zeros of denominators we have
L240: 
L241:  | $\displaystyle\mathcal{F}^{*}(s)$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}}\prod_{p\not|\hskip 2.84526ptq}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}(1+1/p^{k(1+s)})}\right)$  |
L242:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})^{s}/p^{k(1+s)}-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p^{k(1+s)}-2/p^{k}}\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}(1+1/p^{k(1+s)})}\right).$  |
L243: For $s=1,0,-1+1/k$ there are clearly no problems and therefore from the Euler product expressions for the Riemann zeta function
L244:  | $\displaystyle\frac{\zeta(2k)\mathcal{F}^{*}(1)}{\zeta(4k)}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}\prod_{p}\left(\frac{1-p^{-4k}}{1-p^{-2k}}\right)\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{k}(1+1/p^{2k})}\right)$  |
L245:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\prod_{p|q}\frac{1+(q,p^{k})/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}{1+1/p^{2k}-2/p^{k}}\prod_{p}\left(1+\frac{1}{p^{2k}}-\frac{2}{p^{k}}\right),$  |

A variance for k-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus

Tomos Parry

Journal de théorie des nombres de Bordeaux, Tome 33 (2021) no. 2, pp. 317-360

An asymptotic formula for the variance of squarefree numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus was obtained by Nunes, see [9]. We improve one of the error terms as far as one would expect to be able to go.

Une formule asymptotique pour la variance des nombres entiers sans facteur carré dans une progression arithmétique de raison donnée a été trouvée par Nunes dans [9]. Pour l’un des termes d’erreur, nous donnons la meilleure amélioration que l’on puisse espérer d’avoir.

TL;DR: In this article, the distribution of α p modulo one in imaginary quadratic number fields with class number one was investigated, and it was shown that the inequality α p = 1/8+ α p −1/8 + α p is satisfied for infinitely many α p, where α p measures the distance of the vertices of the number field to the ring of integers.

Abstract: We investigate the distribution of $\alpha p$ modulo one in imaginary quadratic number fields $\mathbb{K}\subset\mathbb{C}$ with class number one, where $p$ is restricted to prime elements in the ring of integers $\mathcal{O} = \mathbb{Z}[\omega]$ of $\mathbb{K}$. In analogy to classical work due to R. C. Vaughan, we obtain that the inequality $\lVert\alpha p\rVert_\omega < \mathrm{N}(p)^{-1/8+\epsilon}$ is satisfied for infinitely many $p$, where $\lVert\varrho\rVert_\omega$ measures the distance of $\varrho\in\mathbb{C}$ to $\mathscr{O}$ and $\mathrm{N}(p)$ denotes the norm of $p$. The proof is based on Harman's sieve method and employs number field analogues of classical ideas due to Vinogradov. Moreover, we introduce a smoothing which allows us to make conveniently use of the Poisson summation formula.

Abstract: We construct a tower of fields from the rings $R_n$ which parametrize pairs $(X,\lambda)$, where $X$ is a deformation of a fixed one-dimensional formal group $\mathbb{X}$ of finite height $h$, together with a Drinfeld level-$n$ structure $\lambda$. We choose principal prime ideals $\mathfrak{p}_n \mid (p)$ in each ring $R_n$ in a compatible way and consider the field $K'_n$ obtained by localizing $R_n$ at $\mathfrak{p}_n$, completing, and passing to the fraction field. By taking the compositum $K_n = K'_n K_0$ of each field with the completion $K_0$ of a certain unramified extension of $K'_0$, we obtain a tower of fields $(K_n)_n$ which we prove to be strictly deeply ramified in the sense of Anthony Scholl. When $h=2$ we also investigate the question of whether this is a Kummer tower.

A variance for k-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus

Tomos Parry

Journal de théorie des nombres de Bordeaux, Tome 33 (2021) no. 2, pp. 317-360

An asymptotic formula for the variance of squarefree numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus was obtained by Nunes, see [9]. We improve one of the error terms as far as one would expect to be able to go.

Une formule asymptotique pour la variance des nombres entiers sans facteur carré dans une progression arithmétique de raison donnée a été trouvée par Nunes dans [9]. Pour l’un des termes d’erreur, nous donnons la meilleure amélioration que l’on puisse espérer d’avoir.

TL;DR: In this article, the distribution of α p modulo one in imaginary quadratic number fields with class number one was investigated, and it was shown that the inequality α p = 1/8+ α p −1/8 + α p is satisfied for infinitely many α p, where α p measures the distance of the vertices of the number field to the ring of integers.

...read more read less

[Input]

Abstract: We investigate the distribution of $\alpha p$ modulo one in imaginary quadratic number fields $\mathbb{K}\subset\mathbb{C}$ with class number one, where $p$ is restricted to prime elements in the ring of integers $\mathcal{O} = \mathbb{Z}[\omega]$ of $\mathbb{K}$. In analogy to classical work due to R. C. Vaughan, we obtain that the inequality $\lVert\alpha p\rVert_\omega < \mathrm{N}(p)^{-1/8+\epsilon}$ is satisfied for infinitely many $p$, where $\lVert\varrho\rVert_\omega$ measures the distance of $\varrho\in\mathbb{C}$ to $\mathscr{O}$ and $\mathrm{N}(p)$ denotes the norm of $p$. The proof is based on Harman's sieve method and employs number field analogues of classical ideas due to Vinogradov. Moreover, we introduce a smoothing which allows us to make conveniently use of the Poisson summation formula.

TL;DR: In this article, the authors construct a tower of fields from the rings of a finite one-dimensional formal group, where principal prime ideals are chosen in a compatible way and consider the field obtained by localizing $R_n$ at $\mathfrak{p}_n, completing, and passing to the fraction field.

[Input]

Abstract: We construct a tower of fields from the rings $R_n$ which parametrize pairs $(X,\lambda)$, where $X$ is a deformation of a fixed one-dimensional formal group $\mathbb{X}$ of finite height $h$, together with a Drinfeld level-$n$ structure $\lambda$. We choose principal prime ideals $\mathfrak{p}_n \mid (p)$ in each ring $R_n$ in a compatible way and consider the field $K'_n$ obtained by localizing $R_n$ at $\mathfrak{p}_n$, completing, and passing to the fraction field. By taking the compositum $K_n = K'_n K_0$ of each field with the completion $K_0$ of a certain unramified extension of $K'_0$, we obtain a tower of fields $(K_n)_n$ which we prove to be strictly deeply ramified in the sense of Anthony Scholl. When $h=2$ we also investigate the question of whether this is a Kummer tower.

L239@P4: The question of whether one averages over a complete set of residues,
L240@P4: as here, or over a reduced one, as in [3] and [9], is, most likely harmless
L241@P4: but still remains to be seen. The squarefree numbers are, in contrast to
L242@P4: the primes, not better understood outside the reduced residue classes, and
L243@P4: therefore it isn’t clear, at least to the author, neither why averaging over
L244@P4: a reduced system is guaranteed to be just as insightful as averaging over a
L245@P4: complete system, nor that averaging over a complete system is no harder.
L246@P4: For example, in the reduced residue case, it seems Theorem 2 holds without
L247@P4: the squarefree condition (see Lemma 3.8).
L248@P4: Our argument for Theorem 2 results in replacing the exponent 1/(k + 1)
L249@P4: in the first error term in Theorem 1 with 2k/(9k − 2), and so is inferior
L250@P4: once k ≥ 4, but we could have stated a result for cube-free numbers with
L251@P4: exponent 6/25.
L252@P4: The paper is structured as follows. In Section 2 we carry out the necessary technical work to establish Theorem 1. This is routine and is simply
L253@P4: repeating the outline of the argument in [9] for general k. In Section 3 we
L254@P4: carry out the necessary technical work to establish Theorem 2. Here our
L255@P4: argument is less routine and requires exploiting cancellation in the integrals
L256@P4: arising from applying Perron’s formula. In Section 4 we prove our theorems.

SPARSE VARIANCE FOR PRIMES IN  
ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION

J. BRÜDERN AND T. D. WOOLEY*

**ABSTRACT.** An analogue of the Montgomery-Hooley asymptotic formula is established for the variance of the number of primes in arithmetic progressions, in which the moduli are restricted to the values of a polynomial.

## 1. INTRODUCTION

The distribution of primes is a fundamental problem in the theory of numbers. Our concern here is with the error terms that arise in the prime number theorem for arithmetic progressions. Let φ denote Euler’s totient, and define the relevant quantity \(E(x; k, l)\) for real \(x \ge 2\), and coprime natural numbers \(k\) and \(l\), through the equation

\[
\sum_{\substack{p \le x \\ p \equiv l \bmod k}} \log p = \frac{x}{\phi(k)} + E(x; k, l).
\]

Montgomery [8] obtained an asymptotic formula for the variance

\[
V(x, y) = \sum_{k \le y} \sum_{\substack{l=1 \\ (l,k)=1}}^{k} |E(x; k, l)|^2
\]

ON THE EXPONENTIAL SUM OVER K-FREE NUMBERS

J. Brüdern, A. Granville¹, A. Perelli, R. C. Vaughan² and T. D. Wooley³

**Abstract.** This paper is concerned with mean values of exponential sum generating functions over *k*-free numbers, and especially their *L*¹-means. We also provide non-trivial estimates for the *L*²-means of such generating functions restricted to the minor arcs occurring in Hardy-Littlewood dissections, thereby permitting the circle method to be successfully applied to certain additive problems hitherto beyond its reach.

## 1. Introduction

Applications of the Hardy-Littlewood method to diophantine problems, with variables restricted to inconvenient sets 𝒜, can frequently be much simplified provided that the *L*¹-mean of the exponential sum generated by 𝒜 is suitably small (see §6 for a discussion of this idea). It is therefore a matter of some interest to determine in what circumstances such *L*¹-means are indeed small. It seems that the only non-trivial exponential sums whose *L*¹-means have been investigated hitherto are those corresponding to the von Mangoldt function, Λ, and the Möbius function, μ. Thus, denoting e^{2πiz} by e(z), Vaughan (1988) has shown that

x^{1/2} ≪ ∫₀¹ |∑_{1≤n≤x} Λ(n)e(nα)| dα ≤ (1 + o(1))(x log(2x))^{1/2},

and Balog and Perelli (to appear) have very recently established the bounds

exp(c log x / log log x) ≪ ∫₀¹ |∑_{1≤n≤x} μ(n)e(nα)| dα ≪ x^{1/2},

for a suitable positive number c. In each case the upper bounds, which are believed to lie close to the truth, follow from the corresponding *L*²-means via the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Within the framework of the Hardy-Littlewood method, such a belief implies that a positive proportion of the *L*²-mean must be concentrated on suitably chosen minor arcs. Our primary concern in this paper is to establish bounds for the *L*¹- and *L*²-means of the exponential sum formed with the *k*-free numbers, which is to say the numbers not divisible by any *k*th power of a prime. Our conclusions are in marked contrast with the above cases. When *k* ≥ 2, the *L*¹-mean of this exponential sum is substantially smaller than the bound derived from the *L*²-mean via the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, and the *L*²-mean is concentrated on the major arcs of the Hardy-Littlewood dissection.

In order to describe our first theorem we require some notation. Let μ_k(n) be the characteristic function of the *k*-free numbers, and define f_k(α) = f_k(α; x) by

f_k(α; x) = ∑_{1≤n≤x} μ_k(n)e(nα). (1.1)

SPARSE VARIANCE FOR PRIMES IN  
ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION

J. BRÜDERN AND T. D. WOOLEY*

**ABSTRACT.** An analogue of the Montgomery-Hooley asymptotic formula is established for the variance of the number of primes in arithmetic progressions, in which the moduli are restricted to the values of a polynomial.

## 1. INTRODUCTION

The distribution of primes is a fundamental problem in the theory of numbers. Our concern here is with the error terms that arise in the prime number theorem for arithmetic progressions. Let φ denote Euler’s totient, and define the relevant quantity \(E(x; k, l)\) for real \(x \ge 2\), and coprime natural numbers \(k\) and \(l\), through the equation

\[
\sum_{\substack{p \le x \\ p \equiv l \bmod k}} \log p = \frac{x}{\phi(k)} + E(x; k, l).
\]

Montgomery [8] obtained an asymptotic formula for the variance

\[
V(x, y) = \sum_{k \le y} \sum_{\substack{l=1 \\ (l,k)=1}}^{k} |E(x; k, l)|^2
\]

ON THE EXPONENTIAL SUM OVER K-FREE NUMBERS

J. Brüdern, A. Granville¹, A. Perelli, R. C. Vaughan² and T. D. Wooley³

**Abstract.** This paper is concerned with mean values of exponential sum generating functions over *k*-free numbers, and especially their *L*¹-means. We also provide non-trivial estimates for the *L*²-means of such generating functions restricted to the minor arcs occurring in Hardy-Littlewood dissections, thereby permitting the circle method to be successfully applied to certain additive problems hitherto beyond its reach.

## 1. Introduction

Applications of the Hardy-Littlewood method to diophantine problems, with variables restricted to inconvenient sets 𝒜, can frequently be much simplified provided that the *L*¹-mean of the exponential sum generated by 𝒜 is suitably small (see §6 for a discussion of this idea). It is therefore a matter of some interest to determine in what circumstances such *L*¹-means are indeed small. It seems that the only non-trivial exponential sums whose *L*¹-means have been investigated hitherto are those corresponding to the von Mangoldt function, Λ, and the Möbius function, μ. Thus, denoting e^{2πiz} by e(z), Vaughan (1988) has shown that

x^{1/2} ≪ ∫₀¹ |∑_{1≤n≤x} Λ(n)e(nα)| dα ≤ (1 + o(1))(x log(2x))^{1/2},

and Balog and Perelli (to appear) have very recently established the bounds

exp(c log x / log log x) ≪ ∫₀¹ |∑_{1≤n≤x} μ(n)e(nα)| dα ≪ x^{1/2},

for a suitable positive number c. In each case the upper bounds, which are believed to lie close to the truth, follow from the corresponding *L*²-means via the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Within the framework of the Hardy-Littlewood method, such a belief implies that a positive proportion of the *L*²-mean must be concentrated on suitably chosen minor arcs. Our primary concern in this paper is to establish bounds for the *L*¹- and *L*²-means of the exponential sum formed with the *k*-free numbers, which is to say the numbers not divisible by any *k*th power of a prime. Our conclusions are in marked contrast with the above cases. When *k* ≥ 2, the *L*¹-mean of this exponential sum is substantially smaller than the bound derived from the *L*²-mean via the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, and the *L*²-mean is concentrated on the major arcs of the Hardy-Littlewood dissection.

In order to describe our first theorem we require some notation. Let μ_k(n) be the characteristic function of the *k*-free numbers, and define f_k(α) = f_k(α; x) by

f_k(α; x) = ∑_{1≤n≤x} μ_k(n)e(nα). (1.1)

An analogue of the Montgomery-Hooley asymptotic formula is established for the variance of the number of primes in arithmetic progressions, in which the moduli are restricted to the values of a polynomial.

{
  "summary": "Restrict explicitly to f in Z[t], retaining the original weight f'(k). This includes all three numerical examples and makes the congruence root counts periodic modulo their stated moduli. The simplest route is to sum a published fixed-modulus variance theorem and average its arithmetic factor along f(k). It gives an asymptotic in x^(7/9+delta) <= f(y) <= x^(1-delta), with an explicit logarithmic relative error. Use Tomos Parry's published 2021 Theorem 1, whose constant differs from the problematic displayed constant in the supplied arXiv preprint. The circle-method approach of J. Brüdern and T. D. Wooley, Sparse variance for primes in arithmetic progression (2011), https://www.math.purdue.edu/~twooley/publ/2011sparse.pdf, is unnecessary for this weaker range. No excluded source was consulted or used.",
  "main_theorem": "Let f in Z[t] satisfy all the polynomial hypotheses in problem.md, and let rho be its root-counting function from that file. All logarithms are natural. For each prime p define D_p = 1+p^(-1)-2p^(-2), a_p = (p^(-3/2)-p^(-1))/D_p and b_p = (p^(-2)-p^(-3/2))/D_p. Define C_2 = -4 zeta(-1/2) product_p(1-3p^(-2)+2p^(-3)), where zeta is the Riemann zeta function, and define M_f = product_p(1+a_p rho(p)/p+b_p rho(p^2)/p^2). Both products converge absolutely, and C_f = (2/3) C_2 M_f is positive. For every fixed delta with 0 < delta < 1/9 there is a constant K_{f,delta}>0 such that, uniformly for real x>=3 and integers y>=2 satisfying x^(7/9+delta) <= Y=f(y) <= x^(1-delta), one has |V_f(x,y)-C_f x^(1/2)Y^(3/2)| <= K_{f,delta} x^(1/2)Y^(3/2) log(log(3x))/log(3x).",
  "predicted_main_term": "C_f sqrt(x) f(y)^(3/2), with C_f defined in the main theorem. Products truncated at primes p<=200000 give approximately C_{t^2+1}=0.13808, C_{t^3+2}=0.13561 and C_{2t+1}=0.14261. These decimals are numerical approximations, not certified interval evaluations.",
  "agrees_with_numerics": "Consistent with results.json: the predicted exponents are 1/2 in x and 3/2 in f(y), hence total exponent 2 at fixed f(y)/x. The three predicted constants lie within the file's respective extrapolated intervals 0.13506 +/- 0.01082, 0.14192 +/- 0.01079 and 0.14084 +/- 0.00846. At the smallest reported ratio near 0.01 and the largest x, the normalized observations are approximately 0.14159, 0.14512 and 0.14456. The theorem requires f(y)/x to decrease; it does not predict that the normalized values at fixed positive ratios, including ratio 1, equal C_f. The explicit unrestricted error bound in P6 accommodates such ratio dependence.",
  "propositions": [
    {
      "id": "P1",
      "title": "Identify the progression density",
      "statement": "Let mu denote the Möbius function. For every integer q>=1 and every integer l, the density g(q,l) from problem.md equals the absolutely convergent series sum_{r>=1, gcd(q,r^2)|l} mu(r)/lcm(q,r^2). Equivalently, g(q,l) = (6/(pi^2 q)) product_{p|q}(p^2/(p^2-1)) product_{p||q, p|l}(1-1/p) times the indicator that no prime p satisfies p^2|gcd(q,l). Here p ranges over primes, p||q means p divides q but p^2 does not, and an indicator is 1 when its condition holds and 0 otherwise. These identities hold for every q and l, without a coprimality restriction or an error term.",
      "depends_on": [],
      "cites": [
        "J. Brüdern, A. Granville, A. Perelli, R. C. Vaughan and T. D. Wooley, On the exponential sum over k-free numbers (1998), Lemma 2.1 and equation (2.6), specialized to k=2; https://www.math.purdue.edu/~twooley/publ/1998%20kfree.pdf"
      ],
      "crux": false,
      "risk": "The density must include non-reduced residue classes; replacing it by a constant on all classes would change the variance."
    },
    {
      "id": "P2",
      "title": "Import the published fixed-modulus variance estimate",
      "statement": "For each integer q>=1 define A(q) = product_{p|q}[(1-2p^(-2)+p^(-1)gcd(q,p^2)^(-1/2))/(1+p^(-1)-2p^(-2))], with the empty product equal to 1. Define C_2 = -4 zeta(-1/2) product_p(1-3p^(-2)+2p^(-3)), where zeta denotes the Riemann zeta function and p ranges over primes. For every epsilon>0 there is K_epsilon>0 such that, uniformly for real x>=2 and integers 1<=q<=x, |sum_{l=1}^q E(x;q,l)^2 - C_2 sqrt(xq) A(q)| <= K_epsilon [x^(1/3+epsilon) q^(2/3) + x^(5/3+epsilon)/q]. The E in this statement is exactly the error defined in problem.md, including every residue class.",
      "depends_on": [
        "P1"
      ],
      "cites": [
        "Tomos Parry, A variance for k-free numbers in arithmetic progressions of given modulus (2021), Theorem 1, specialized to k=2; https://jtnb.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/jtnb.1163.pdf"
      ],
      "crux": false,
      "risk": "Use the published theorem and its constant, not the supplied preprint's displayed Euler product. Check that the average is over all residue classes and that the bound is uniform down to q=1."
    },
    {
      "id": "P3",
      "title": "Local arithmetic factor and its convergent polynomial mean",
      "statement": "Fix f in Z[t] satisfying problem.md. For each prime p put D_p=1+p^(-1)-2p^(-2), a_p=(p^(-3/2)-p^(-1))/D_p and b_p=(p^(-2)-p^(-3/2))/D_p. For integers q>=1 define A(q)=product_p(1+a_p 1_{p|q}+b_p 1_{p^2|q}), where 1_condition denotes its indicator. For real z>=2 define A_z(q) by restricting this product to p<=z, and define M_f(z)=product_{p<=z}(1+a_p rho(p)/p+b_p rho(p^2)/p^2). Then M_f=lim_{z->infinity} M_f(z) exists as an absolutely convergent positive product. There is K_f>0 such that |M_f-M_f(z)|<=K_f/z for every real z>=2. Uniformly for integers q>=1 and real z>=2, 0<A(q)<=A_z(q)<=1 and |A(q)-A_z(q)| <= sum_{p>z, p|q} 1/p. Moreover A_z(f(k)) is periodic in the integer k with period N_z=product_{p<=z}p^2, and its average over one complete period is exactly M_f(z).",
      "depends_on": [],
      "cites": [],
      "crux": false,
      "risk": "Primes dividing every coefficient of f require separate finite local treatment. Repeated polynomial factors are allowed; a bound for rho(p^2) must not assume nonsingular roots."
    },
    {
      "id": "P4",
      "title": "Elementary averaging along polynomial values",
      "statement": "Fix f in Z[t] satisfying problem.md, and let c_f be the positive greatest common divisor of its coefficients. For primes p define D_p=1+p^(-1)-2p^(-2), a_p=(p^(-3/2)-p^(-1))/D_p and b_p=(p^(-2)-p^(-3/2))/D_p. Define A(q)=product_p(1+a_p 1_{p|q}+b_p 1_{p^2|q}) for integers q>=1, where 1_condition is its indicator, and M_f=product_p(1+a_p rho(p)/p+b_p rho(p^2)/p^2). There is K_f>0 such that, uniformly for real u>=2 and real z>=max(2,c_f), |sum_{1<=k<=u} A(f(k))-u M_f| <= K_f [u/z+log(2f(u))+z^(2z)]. In particular, after choosing z=log(u)/(8 log(log(u))) whenever u is large enough that this is at least max(2,c_f), and enlarging K_f to cover the remaining u>=2, one has |sum_{1<=k<=u} A(f(k))-u M_f| <= K_f u log(log(3u))/log(3u). All sums over k are over positive integers.",
      "depends_on": [
        "P3"
      ],
      "cites": [],
      "crux": true,
      "risk": "The large-prime tail must be averaged before estimating it. A pointwise tail bound alone is inadequate. The periodic averaging error must retain the full period, bounded here explicitly by z^(2z); no equidistribution assertion for growing moduli is assumed."
    },
    {
      "id": "P5",
      "title": "Weighted mean and polynomial summation bounds",
      "statement": "Fix f in Z[t] satisfying problem.md. For primes p define D_p=1+p^(-1)-2p^(-2), a_p=(p^(-3/2)-p^(-1))/D_p and b_p=(p^(-2)-p^(-3/2))/D_p. Put A(q)=product_p(1+a_p 1_{p|q}+b_p 1_{p^2|q}), with indicators taking values 0 or 1, and M_f=product_p(1+a_p rho(p)/p+b_p rho(p^2)/p^2). There is K_f>0 such that, uniformly for every integer y>=2, with Y=f(y), |sum_{k=1}^y f'(k) sqrt(f(k)) A(f(k))-(2/3)M_f Y^(3/2)| <= K_f Y^(3/2) log(log(3y))/log(3y). In the same range, sum_{k=1}^y f'(k) f(k)^(2/3) <= K_f Y^(5/3) and sum_{k=1}^y f'(k)/f(k) <= K_f log(2Y). The constant depends only on the fixed polynomial f.",
      "depends_on": [
        "P4"
      ],
      "cites": [],
      "crux": false,
      "risk": "Partial summation must control the variation of f'(t)sqrt(f(t)); it need not be increasing on the entire initial interval. The discrete endpoint contribution must be included in the displayed error."
    },
    {
      "id": "P6",
      "title": "Assemble the quantitative sparse variance formula",
      "statement": "Fix f in Z[t] satisfying problem.md. For primes p define D_p=1+p^(-1)-2p^(-2), a_p=(p^(-3/2)-p^(-1))/D_p and b_p=(p^(-2)-p^(-3/2))/D_p. Define C_f=-(8/3) zeta(-1/2) product_p(1-3p^(-2)+2p^(-3)) product_p(1+a_p rho(p)/p+b_p rho(p^2)/p^2), where zeta is the Riemann zeta function. For every epsilon>0 there is K_{f,epsilon}>0 such that, uniformly for real x>=2 and integers y>=2 with Y=f(y)<=x, |V_f(x,y)-C_f sqrt(x)Y^(3/2)| <= K_{f,epsilon}[sqrt(x)Y^(3/2) log(log(3y))/log(3y) + x^(1/3+epsilon)Y^(5/3) + x^(5/3+epsilon)log(2Y)]. Consequently, for each fixed 0<delta<1/9 there is K_{f,delta}>0 such that, uniformly for x>=3 and integers y>=2 satisfying x^(7/9+delta)<=Y=f(y)<=x^(1-delta), the left-hand side is at most K_{f,delta} sqrt(x)Y^(3/2) log(log(3x))/log(3x). Constants are independent of x and y.",
      "depends_on": [
        "P2",
        "P5"
      ],
      "cites": [],
      "crux": false,
      "risk": "The accumulated x^(5/3+epsilon)/q error creates the lower threshold 7/9. The accumulated first error prevents a vanishing relative error at fixed positive Y/x; the conclusion must not be extended to that regime."
    }
  ]
}
